channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: How KazAgroFinance Helps Farmers Purchase Agricultural Machinery
item.description: KazAgroFinance, part of the Baiterek holding, offers leasing options for farmers to acquire agricultural machinery, allowing payments to be spread over several years. The recent KazAgroFarm exhibition in Astana showcased new technologies and equipment from 25 countries, facilitating direct interaction between farmers and manufacturers.

item.title: Pakistani Jets Bomb Taliban Base in Afghanistan's Paktika Province
item.description: Pakistani fighter jets reportedly bombed a Taliban military base in the Shakin district of Paktika province, near the Angoor Ada border crossing. The base was reportedly abandoned by the Taliban three months prior. This incident follows several clashes between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces along the border.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases After Four Days of Growth
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen after a four-day increase. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 31. The data indicates a slight decrease in the dollar's value.

item.title: Almaty Health Minister Orders Probe into Drug Procurement and Pharmacy Sales
item.description: Kazakhstan's Health Minister Akmaral Alnazarova has ordered a thorough investigation into the procurement of medicines by Almaty medical organizations and their subsequent sale in pharmacies. The probe will examine the legality of purchases made outside the designated unified distributor system and the illicit sale of free medications. The minister emphasized transparency in drug supply and adherence to procurement rules.

item.title: Eurasian Bank Drops to Ninth Place in Kazakhstan's Largest Banks Ranking
item.description: Eurasian Bank has fallen from eighth to ninth position among Kazakhstan's largest banks by assets, overtaken by Bank RBK. As of September 2026, Bank RBK's assets grew by nearly 120 billion tenge in one month, reaching 2.893 trillion tenge, while Eurasian Bank's assets decreased by 42 billion tenge to 2.809 trillion tenge. Eurasian Bank has lost two positions since the beginning of the year.

item.title: Over 360 Graffiti and Drug Advertisement Markings Removed in Astana
item.description: Astana has conducted an 'Anti-Vandal' campaign, removing over 360 instances of graffiti and illegal drug advertisement markings from public spaces. Volunteers and students participated in cleaning playgrounds and walls. The 'Astana Zhasylary' youth center reported organizing over 40 such events, with volunteers conducting weekly raids to identify and remove vandalism across the city.

item.title: Binance Reserves Over $6.34 Billion to Cover Losses from Hacker Attack
item.description: Following a hacker attack that resulted in the theft of cryptocurrencies valued between $1.7 billion and $5.5 billion, the international crypto exchange Binance has reserved over $6.34 billion from its own funds to cover user losses. The company has begun efforts to restore assets for affected users.

item.title: Kazakhstan Uncovers Drug Network, Seizes Crypto Assets Worth Over 2 Billion Tenge
item.description: Authorities in Astana have dismantled four online drug stores, leading to convictions with sentences of 16 to 17 years. During the investigation, 88 crypto wallets containing assets exceeding 2 billion tenge were discovered. The criminal groups were involved in selling drugs via the internet, with members fulfilling roles from organization and financing to distribution.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Electricity Usage Rules Effective November 8
item.description: New regulations for connecting to electricity, replacing meters, and calculating electricity bills in Kazakhstan will take effect on November 8. The changes apply to both individuals and businesses. The Ministry of Energy signed the order amending the rules on October 16.

item.title: New Polio Vaccination Campaign to Commence Across Afghanistan on Monday
item.description: A new round of polio vaccination campaigns is set to begin across Afghanistan on Monday, announced the Polio Free Afghanistan initiative. The campaign in the southern zone will start a day later, on Tuesday, November 3. UNICEF reports that 12.7 million children have been vaccinated so far.

item.title: Highest Salaries for Working Pensioners in Kazakhstan Found in Foreign Companies
item.description: Working pensioners in Kazakhstan aged over 65 earn the highest salaries in foreign companies, averaging over 477,000 tenge monthly. State enterprises pay an average of 313,274 tenge, while Kazakhstani private companies offer 364,105 tenge. Foreign firms' average salaries are about 52% higher than state ones.

item.title: Uzbekistan emphasizes safety measures for increased energy use in autumn-winter
item.description: Uzbekistan is conducting awareness campaigns to prevent incidents during the autumn-winter period, when demand for electricity and natural gas increases. Emphasis is placed on the correct use of gas equipment, checking heating devices, and cleaning chimneys. 'Bukhara Gas' branch recommends regular checks and adherence to manufacturer instructions for safe operation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Seeks Stronger Strategic Partnership with Turkey, President Japarov Meets Erdogan
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. Japarov expressed gratitude for the warm reception and high-level organization of the Turkic States Summit. He emphasized Kyrgyzstan's interest in enhancing its comprehensive strategic partnership with Turkey, noting broad opportunities for increased interaction in mutually beneficial areas.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Initiatives on Industry, Logistics, Tourism, and Visa-Free Travel at Turkic States Summit
item.description: At the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan put forward proposals concerning industry, logistics, tourism, and visa-free travel. The summit, held under the theme "Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action," was attended by leaders from member states and observers. Mirziyoyev expressed gratitude for Turkey's organization and highlighted the opening of a national-cultural complex.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Pension Savings Transfer to Private Management Companies
item.description: Kazakh citizens can now transfer 100% of their pension savings to private management companies, choosing who manages and invests their funds. Experts explain how to select a suitable management company. This option, expanded in 2023, has seen increased interest, with over 180,000 contributors transferring approximately 179 billion tenge by August 31, 2026.

item.title: Astana drug ring organizers and participants receive up to 17 years imprisonment
item.description: Organizers and participants of drug trafficking rings in Astana have been sentenced to up to 17 years in prison. Three verdicts have come into force, with 18 individuals convicted. Funds, digital assets, property, and vehicles were confiscated.

item.title: Eldor Arippov outlines priorities for Central Asia-EU strategic partnership
item.description: The first Forum of Think Tanks of Central Asia and the European Union was held in Brussels, focusing on transforming cooperation in a changing world. Director of ISMI Eldor Arippov highlighted the growing importance of Central Asia in European foreign policy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Stricter Accountability for Gambling Business Leaders
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to amend financial monitoring rules for gambling and lottery organizers. New regulations would hold company leaders and responsible employees personally liable for violations. The Ministry of Tourism and Sport stated these changes align Kazakhstan's legislation with international standards, including recommendations from the Financial Action Task Force.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Preferential Trade Agreement, Sign Business and Social Security Pacts
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey have agreed to expand their preferential trade list, adding eight new products each. Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed agreements on business support and social security in Ankara. The countries aim to increase bilateral trade from $3.25 billion to $5 billion by January 2026 and $10 billion in the medium term.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Self-Employed Individuals Will Not Be Fined for Lack of Employment Contract
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection clarified that self-employed individuals will not face administrative penalties solely for not having an employment contract. Employers who misuse self-employment status to avoid labor obligations will be held responsible. The ministry emphasized the distinction between labor contracts and self-employment.

item.title: United Airlines Considers Flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, Faces Russian Airspace Restrictions
item.description: United Airlines is exploring the possibility of launching flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan but is currently unable to due to restrictions on using Russian airspace. The airline's CEO mentioned that a dedicated team is researching new routes and their viability. While direct flights are not yet feasible, the company remains open to future opportunities.

item.title: Central Asia Electricity Demand to Rise 27% by 2030, Eurasian Development Bank Projects
item.description: Electricity demand in Central Asia is projected to increase by 27% by 2030, according to the Eurasian Development Bank (EDB). The EDB emphasizes the need to prepare generation capacity and power grids now to support economic growth and prevent energy shortages. The report also calls for grid upgrades and investment in energy storage.

item.title: Turkic States Summit in Ankara: Kazakhstan Proposes Inviting Russia
item.description: At the 13th summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Ankara, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed inviting Russia to join the organization or participate as an observer. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan emphasized unity and cooperation within the Turkic world. Turkey assumed the rotating presidency of the OTS from Azerbaijan.

item.title: Kazakh President Concludes Official Visit to Turkey
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has concluded his official visit to Turkey. He was seen off at Ankara airport by Turkey's Minister of Trade, Omer Bolat. During the visit, Tokayev attended the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States and participated in the opening of the Turkic World Alley in Ankara.

item.title: OrdaMed Fraud Case, Causing 4.5 Billion Tenge Damage, Reaches Almaty Court
item.description: A case involving fictitious production of medical devices by OrdaMed, causing 4.5 billion tenge in damages, has been filed in the Almaty court. The company allegedly obtained illegal preferences by using fake production documents, while importing equipment from abroad. OrdaMed denies the accusations.

item.title: Rogun Hydropower Plant Accident: Conflicting Reports on Worker Injuries Emerge
item.description: An accident at Tajikistan's Rogun Hydropower Plant on October 21 involved a water tank rupture, with conflicting reports on worker injuries. Authorities claim no one was hurt, while witnesses report over five injured. The incident occurred in a construction tunnel affecting workers from Sinohydro.

item.title: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Cyberattack Amid Central Asia Expansion
item.description: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, reported a cyberattack on October 29, resulting in the theft of approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets. The company is freezing assets and suspending withdrawals while investigating the incident, which may have originated from a compromised engineer's laptop. Binance pledged to cover all losses. This attack occurs as Binance expands its operations in Central Asia, including licensed exchanges in Kazakhstan and cooperation with Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Turkish Intelligence Captures Suspected Daesh Operative in Afghanistan-Pakistan Region
item.description: Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MIT) has captured a suspected member of the Daesh terrorist group operating in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region. The suspect, identified as Uğur Bahadır, also known by the alias Abdullah, was allegedly involved with Daesh's Khorasan branch (ISKP). Security sources confirmed the operative has been transferred to Turkey.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tenge Weakens Against US Dollar, Reaching 453.87 Tenge
item.description: The US dollar strengthened against the Kazakhstan Tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE), with the average exchange rate reaching 453.87 tenge, an increase of 0.27 tenge. The National Bank's official rate was set at 453.71 tenge. Exchange rates in Astana and Almaty showed similar trends, with the dollar trading around 456.99 tenge in Astana and 454.73 tenge in Almaty.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Ban Electricity Payments for Drinking Water Debtors
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to restrict electricity payments for individuals with outstanding drinking water debts. This new regulation is expected to come into effect from January 1, 2027. The measure aims to improve payment discipline for essential utilities.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Central Asia Education Cooperation Program Until 2030
item.description: At a Tashkent forum, Tajikistan proposed developing a regional roadmap for education and science cooperation for 2027-2030. Education ministers from Central Asian nations attended, discussing academic exchange, joint programs, and mutual recognition of qualifications. The initiative aims to strengthen regional collaboration.

item.title: Qatar Mediates Iran-US Talks Amidst Unacceptable Peace Proposal
item.description: Qatari mediators have arrived in Tehran for talks between the United States and Iran, coordinated with Washington. A Qatari peace proposal was presented to Iran, but a senior Iranian official deemed it unacceptable, stating Tehran would maintain its nuclear stance. Washington seeks to include Iran's nuclear program in negotiations.

item.title: UN General Assembly Adopts "Samarkand Vision – 2040" as Official Document
item.description: The final document of the V Samarkand Human Rights Forum, "Samarkand Vision – 2040: Global Cooperation for Human Dignity, Equality, and Sustainable Development," has been adopted as an official document of the 81st UN General Assembly session. Published in six UN official languages, it includes a roadmap for implementation.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Cooperation with Third Countries within Turkic States Organization
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed initiating cooperation with third countries within the Turkic States Organization (TMT) during the Ankara summit. He suggested a "TMT Plus" format, starting with sectoral ministers' meetings, to foster practical joint projects in trade, transport, and investment.

item.title: Public hearings on oncology held in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Public hearings on oncology were held in the Republic of Karakalpakstan, focusing on cancer prevention, early detection, and improving healthcare services. The event, part of the "Uzbekistan-2030" strategy, included participation from the Ministry of Health, oncologists, and civil society representatives. Reports on preventive measures and screening results were presented.

item.title: Cybercrime awareness meeting held for students in Nukus
item.description: An educational meeting on cybersecurity was held for students at the Ajiniyaz Nukus State Pedagogical Institute. The event aimed to raise awareness about online threats, internet fraud, and cybercrime prevention. Representatives from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the institute discussed digital literacy and safe internet usage.

item.title: Uzbek Deputy Foreign Minister Mirvohid Azimov Appointed Secretary General of Organization of Turkic States
item.description: Mirvohid Azimov, Uzbekistan's Deputy Foreign Minister, has been appointed Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) by a decision of the Council of Heads of State at the 13th summit in Ankara. This marks the first time an Uzbek representative holds this position. Azimov previously served as Deputy Secretary General of the OTS.

item.title: Uzbek President Outlines Vision for Turkic States Organization at Ankara Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed strengthening cooperation within the Turkic States Organization (TDT), viewing it as a platform for mutual trust and practical partnership. He suggested joint initiatives in technology, industry, and resource processing, including a "Turkic World 100" program for strategic projects.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Develop Textbook Publishing Program for 2027-2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to develop a state program for publishing textbooks and educational materials for schools for the period 2027-2030. Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Ulan Mamatkanov emphasized the need to digitize the entire process, from ordering to distribution, and improve the expertise system.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Gasoline Reserves by 2.5 Times Ahead of Winter Season
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has increased its gasoline reserves at oil depots by 2.5 times compared to the same period last year. The company stated that its gas stations are supplied for the upcoming winter. The deputy chairman for processing, Abrorjon Khudoyberganov, announced this at a press conference on October 27. The company has expanded its network of gas stations and increased sales volume.
